target.title: fix(acp): catch unhandled rejection from handleGatewayEvent in event callback
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The ACP server passes Gateway events to the async translator from a synchronous `onEvent` callback and discards the returned Promise. `GatewayClient` catches synchronous callback throws, but a later translator rejection could escape as an unhandled rejection and terminate the ACP process.

## Why This Change Was Made

Contain the rejection where the Promise becomes fire-and-forget: `src/acp/server.ts`. This keeps `AcpGatewayAgent.handleGatewayEvent` rejectable for direct callers and tests, emits one low-noise stderr diagnostic in normal mode, and adds error detail only with `--verbose`. The shape matches the existing MCP Gateway event boundary.

## User Impact

Unexpected ACP Gateway event-processing failures no longer leak as unhandled rejections. The failure remains observable without contaminating stdout's protocol stream.

## Evidence

- Final head: `b56685db3fcdbf88ea9e074359df361016930455`; diff is limited to `src/acp/server.ts` and `src/acp/server.startup.test.ts`.
- Boundary regression coverage dispatches through the captured Gateway callback and verifies default and verbose diagnostics.
- Sanitized direct AWS Crabbox (`cbx_465b389a6764`, public network, no Tailscale), run `run_ffdf3ab9b715` on pre-rebase head `5af84e1642c134f4f5a9bd34ee76b3a6c64c4e16`: `pnpm test src/acp/server.startup.test.ts src/acp/translator.error-kind.test.ts` — 17/17 passed on Node 24. Both runtime/test blobs are identical on the final rebase.
- Fresh final-head AutoReview: clean, confidence 0.86.
- Hosted CI is running on the rewritten head; native prepare remains the landing gate.

Contributor report and original implementation credited to @ajwan8998; maintainer fixup moves the catch to the server-owned callback boundary. Release notes are deferred to the repository's release-owned changelog flow.
